item.title: Iran War Live Updates: U.S. and Iran Trade Proposals on Nuclear Restrictions
item.summary: Iran said it could suspend uranium enrichment for up to five years but the Trump administration insisted on 20 years, officials from both countries said.

item.title: As War Chills Economy, Dubai’s Most Vulnerable Bear the Cost
item.summary: Migrant workers in the United Arab Emirates, whose hospitality industry has been hit hard by the war with Iran, are facing furloughs, pay cuts and even repatriation.

item.title: As Bahrain Cracked Down Amid War, a Death in Custody Sparked Outrage
item.summary: The body of a man accused of spying for Iran, Mohammed al-Mousawi, showed signs of torture, witnesses said. The U.N. has called for an investigation.

item.title: Europe Is Desperate for More Energy. Can Norway Come to the Rescue?
item.summary: The war in Iran has once again exposed Europe’s energy vulnerability. A friendly source at home would seem to be ideal. But it’s not that easy.

item.title: Israelis Don’t Feel Much Like Victors in War With Iran
item.summary: The regime in Iran has not changed and the nuclear and missile threats have not been eliminated, leaving many Israelis to wonder what this was all for.

item.title: State of U.S. Blockade Is Unclear as Some Ships Transit Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: Ship-tracking data showed that several vessels, including some that had been docked at Iranian ports, had moved through the strait as the U.S. military began its blockade.

item.title: Ex-Student Wounds 16 in High School Shooting in Turkey
item.summary: Officials said the teenage attacker killed himself when cornered by the police. The authorities are investigating possible motives.

item.title: Israel and Lebanon Seek Way Forward in Rare Direct Talks
item.summary: The talks, set for Tuesday in Washington, were not expected to produce an immediate breakthrough in the war between Hezbollah and Israel.

item.title: Will Viktor Orban’s Legacy Live On in Brussels, Even Without Him?
item.summary: Viktor Orban, Hungary’s newly ousted prime minister, helped to finance a Brussels think tank that pushes his populist vision. It will outlast him, at least for a while.

item.title: Adopted by Denmark, a Bombed-Out Ukrainian City Is Given New Life
item.summary: The Danish government has contributed more than $250 million to Mykolaiv, as the Trump administration pushes a more business-focused plan.
